What if humans could breathe underwater? No tank. No mask. Just gills.
First problem. Water holds about thirty times less oxygen than air. So your gills would have to be enormous.
Second problem. Water steals your body heat twenty-five times faster than air. So we'd need blubber. Like a seal.
But then, the whole ocean opens up. Seventy percent of the planet. Cities on the sea floor. Kelp farms. Dolphins for neighbours.
And nobody would ever drown again.
Just one catch. Below two hundred metres, there is no sunlight at all. And down there, we are not the top of the food chain.
Would you live underwater? Tell me below.
